newsitem.title: DUBAI: APICORP, Saudi banks in $160 mln Texaco loan.
newsitem.headline: APICORP, Saudi banks in $160 mln Texaco loan.

text.p: The Arab Petroleum Investments Corp (APICORP) said on Wednesday it was taking part in a $160 million loan to Saudi Arabian Texaco, a unit of Texaco Inc, to finance investment in the neutral zone between Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.
APICORP said in a statement it was co-financing the loan with Riyad Bank and Saudi Hollandi Bank, which is 40 percent owned by ABN-Amro Bank.
"This facility was guaranteed by Texaco Inc," it said.
Banking sources said the banks had agreed to provide the facility on December 7 and the agreement was signed with Texaco on December 16.
They refused to disclose the rate above LIBOR at which the loan was fixed but said it would be issued in three tranches.

Two would be used to refinance two existing loans of around $85 million, they said. The third tranche would help rebuild some of Saudi Arabian Texaco's installations which had been damaged in the 1991 Gulf War, they added.
Saudi Arabian Texaco and Kuwait Oil Co (KOC) share onshore oil production in the neutral zone.

Kuwaiti officials said in October that Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Saudi Arabian Texaco had agreed to spend $400 million to raise output from onshore fields in the neutral zone to 300,000 barrels per day by 1998 from a current 190,000 to 200,00 bpd.
